core_meaning.primary_meaning: Ansar corresponds to the Arabic form أنصار and is glossed in this record as “Helpers, supporters.” The record associates the form with root ن ص ر (n-ṣ-r). The record identifies the form as plural. The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Ansar corresponds to the Arabic form أنصار (Arabic root ن ص ر (n-ṣ-r); أَنْصَار (ʾanṣār)). Its core sense is helpers; supporters. Ansar is Arabic أَنْصَار (ʾanṣār) 'Helpers, supporters', the broken plural of the active participle of نَصَرَ (naṣara, 'to help') from the root ن ص ر (n-ṣ-r).

etymology.morphology: Broken plural (afʿāl pattern) of the active participle of نَصَرَ (naṣara, 'to help'), built on the root ن ص ر.
etymology.etymological_meaning: From the root ن ص ر (n-ṣ-r)
etymology.etymology_explanation: The form أنصار is an established Arabic lexical item — the plural of the helper form of the root ن ص ر — and Ansar is the word itself used as a personal name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: No derivation beyond the documented Arabic form is asserted. Any etymology that attributes this spelling to a different root or language without a source should be treated as unverified.

persian.name: أنصار

faq.a: Documented usage records Ansar as a boy's name; actual use can vary by community.
